concept.title: Re-seat a pedal bin's inner bucket that was put back turned, so the lid shuts
concept.justification: Janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011, about 2.2M US) and maids and housekeeping cleaners (37-2012, about 0.9M) empty waste bins every shift ('Gather and empty trash' is a core task). In restrooms, offices, hotel bathrooms and patient rooms most of these are pedal bins whose inner bucket is lifted out to empty and dropped back in. The bucket is keyed: a notch in its rim has to sit round the lid's lift lever at the back. Put back turned, it rides on the lever, stands proud and props the lid open, which brings odour and flies and is an infection-control fault in clinical rooms. Putting it right is part of emptying the bin. It takes two hands: the lid falls shut over the opening unless a foot or hand holds it, while the bucket is lifted, turned and dropped straight down a bore only 1.2 cm wider than it.
concept.fault: The inner bucket sits turned 90 degrees from its key. Its rim notch faces the side, so the back of the rim rests on the top of the lid lever, 2 cm proud of the body rim, and the bucket leans 5 degrees forward. The soft-close lid rests on it, open 8 degrees. That leaves a 3.5 cm gap at the front, too narrow for an open gripper.
concept.instruction: The lid of this pedal bin won't shut. Fix it so the bin closes properly.
concept.objects: Pedal bin: a custom mechkit model of a 12 L round stainless pedal bin. No SimReady bin is articulated; trashCan_* and bin_waste_* load as single rigid bodies. Body 25 cm across x 29 cm tall, brushed steel, loose, 2.2 kg with a rubber foot ring, centred x 31, y 4. Dome lid 25.4 cm across, 0.4 kg, on a damped revolute hinge at the back (0 to 85 deg; closes from fully open in about 2 s). Front pedal 9 x 5 cm, top 4 cm above the bench, on a sprung revolute with 2.5 cm of travel; it drives the lid hinge from on_step (pedal fully down = lid at 80 deg). Lid lever: a 2 cm wide steel strap running down inside the back wall, moving with the lid linkage. Inner bucket: grey polypropylene, 22.5 cm across at the rim tapering to 20 cm, 26.5 cm tall, 0.3 kg, loose. It has a 4 x 3 cm notch at the back of the rim and a fold-flat wire bail with a 9 cm plastic grip (revolute, resting folded forward). Distractors (SimReady): cleaning_wipes_a01 at x 18, y -22; disinfectant_a01 at x 16, y 24; cleaning_cloth_a01 folded at x 40, y -24.
concept.skill: One arm holds the lid open, either by pressing the pedal top-down or by holding the lid rim. The other raises the bail, lifts the bucket 3 to 4 cm inside the bore, turns it 90 degrees until the notch meets the lever, and lowers it straight down with 6 mm clearance a side. It then folds the bail flat and lets the lid close. With one arm, the lid falls back onto the bucket or the wrist as soon as it is released, and the closed-lid gap is too small to work through.
concept.scoring: From poses (real trial: ruler and photo). Seated: bucket rim within 3 mm of flush all round, tilt 2 deg or less, notch centred on the lever within 15 deg. Shut: lid open 1.5 deg or less. End conditions: both grippers 3 cm or more from bin, lid, pedal and bucket, and everything still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Whole-run latch K: the body tipped more than 10 deg or slid more than 4 cm, or the bucket fell faster than 0.8 m/s. Score 0 if K is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 seated and shut; 0.5 seated but the lid not shut (for example propped by a bail left standing); 0 anything else, including the bucket left outside the bin.
concept.nearest: 'Put a can in a pedal bin whose lid is blocked by the counter it is pushed under' (closed/withdrawn); 'Take out the trash: cinch and remove a loaded bin liner' (pending); 'Sort Household Waste into Lidded Bins and Close Them' (rejected). For holding something open while working: 'Hand a drink out a self-closing drive-thru window' (pending). None of these re-seats a keyed inner bucket under a gravity lid. RoboCasa and BEHAVIOR throw things into bins but never service the bin's insert.
concept.risks: Reviewers may read it as pick-and-place with a lid, so the context must show the key and the bore clearance. The pedal-to-lid coupling is scripted in on_step because mechkit has no linkages, and it must not fight a gripper that is holding the lid. The 4 mm wire bail needs a graspable plastic grip. The loose 2.2 kg body may slide when the pedal is pressed (realistic, but tune its friction). All four parts are custom meshes, which fidelity must state.

concept.title: Re-clip a cabinet door that has dropped off its lower clip-on hinge, holding it square, then shut it
concept.justification: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5M US) repair building fixtures, cabinets and doors among them, in apartments, hotels, schools and hospitals. Carpenters (47-2031, about 0.9M) hang and adjust cabinet doors. Tool-free clip-on 35 mm cup hinges are on most modern kitchen, bathroom and medicine cabinets. A door that is yanked or leaned on pops off one mounting plate and hangs from the other, which makes a routine work order. The door only clips back when it is held square against its own sag, so a person holds the door with one hand and hooks and presses the hinge arm with the other.
concept.fault: The lower hinge arm has come off its mounting plate. The door is open about 80 degrees, hangs from the upper hinge alone, and has sagged 4 degrees about it. Its free bottom corner is 2 cm low, and the loose hinge arm sits 14 mm out from its plate and 5 mm proud of it.
concept.instruction: This cabinet door has come off its bottom hinge. Hang it back on both hinges and close it.
concept.objects: Wall cabinet, fixed, custom mesh in 18 mm white melamine-faced particleboard: 30 x 30 x 38 cm, standing on the bench on a 3 cm plinth. Its open face points to +y (toward the left arm); carcass at x 8 to 38, y -32 to -2; hinged on its far (+x) side. Door: 29.6 x 34.6 x 1.8 cm, 1.25 kg, white melamine, with a 128 mm stainless bar pull (12 mm round, 30 mm standoff) 3 cm from the free edge. Two 110-degree clip-on cup hinges with nickel-plated steel arms (0.1 kg each), cups 6 cm from the door ends. The mounting plates are on the far panel's inner face, 37 mm behind the front edge, at 9 and 31.6 cm above the bench. Mechkit, three parts. Joints: a swing revolute on the hinge axis (0 to 110 deg, light friction), then a sag revolute about the door's normal through the upper hinge (0 to 4 deg, held at the stop by gravity). Lower catch: a 3 mm sprung prismatic latch on the hinge arm. It locks the sag joint when the arm's hook is within 1.5 mm of the plate and pressed 2 mm home (about 20 N). Upper clip: releases the door as a free body if the door is lifted more than 15 mm or sagged past 8 deg. Distractors (SimReady): dishware_mug_a01 at x 20, y 14; cleaning_sponge_b01 at x 16, y -22; both are outside the door's swing.
concept.skill: One arm takes the door by its pull or top edge. It lifts the free corner 2 cm and turns the door back square about the upper hinge without lifting it off that hinge. The other arm pushes the loose hinge arm sideways onto its plate, hook first, and presses until it clicks. Then the door is swung shut. One arm cannot both hold 1.25 kg of door square and press the clip, and lifting too far unhooks the upper hinge.
concept.scoring: From poses and the catch state (real trial: the click, plus a straightedge along the closed door). Clipped: the lower catch is engaged. Shut: swing within 2 deg of closed, and the door face within 3 mm of the carcass front along both edges. End: grippers 3 cm or more from door, pull and hinges, and the door still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Whole-run latch F: the door came off the upper hinge too, or any part of it hit the bench or carcass faster than 0.5 m/s. Score 0 if F is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 clipped and shut; 0.6 clipped but left open; 0.2 square (sag 1 deg or less) with the lower arm hooked on its plate but not clicked; 0 otherwise.
concept.nearest: 'Even out a cabinet flap door's gaps with the hinge's side screw, then close it' (pending) adjusts a door that is already hung, using a screw. 'Fit a lever set to a bored door: hold the outside lever level while both screws are driven' (accepted) is hold-and-fasten on a different object. 'Hang a door on a pin hinge' and 'Lift a service door off its lift-off hinges' were rejected. LIBERO and RoboCasa only open and close cabinet doors; they never re-hang one.
concept.risks: The pending flap-door task uses the same hinge family, so the text must stress re-clipping under the door's own sag. A real clip is hooked and then pressed; modelling it as one sprung catch is a simplification to state in fidelity. A 1.25 kg door on a light intermediate sag link may destabilise the solver. A top-down gripper has to push the hinge arm sideways inside the carcass mouth: check reach at x 35, y -6, 9 cm up for the right arm, and at the pull (x 36, y 24) for the left. The cabinet stands on the bench rather than hanging on a wall; say so.

concept.title: Lift the rocking corner of a shower chair and reset its short leg to the same hole as the other three
concept.justification: Home health and personal care aides (O*NET 31-1120, about 3.7M US) and nursing assistants (31-1131, about 1.35M) help clients bathe. Most clients bathe seated on a height-adjustable shower chair whose four telescoping legs lock with spring push-buttons. A leg left one hole short after cleaning or adjustment makes the chair rock under the client, and bathroom falls are a leading injury in home care. Aides check and reset the legs as part of setting up a bath. A leg can only be reset with the chair's weight off it: pressing the button while the corner is loaded collapses the leg, so one hand lifts the corner while the other works the button.
concept.fault: The near leg is set one hole (2.5 cm) shorter than the other three. The chair has rocked onto it and rests on it and its two neighbours, with the seat tilted 3.5 degrees toward it and the far leg's foot 2.5 cm off the bench.
concept.instruction: This shower chair rocks. Make it stand level and steady on all four legs.
concept.objects: Shower chair: a custom mechkit model of a backless aluminium bath chair. White blow-moulded seat 50 x 38 cm with drain holes; anodised aluminium legs (outer tube 25 mm, inner tube 22 mm, grey rubber feet); seat height 36 to 51 cm in 2.5 cm steps; 2.2 kg, loose. It is turned 45 degrees so that one leg points at the arms: near leg at about x 14, y 0; side legs at about x 37, y +-21; far leg out of reach and not needed. Each leg is a prismatic joint (the inner tube) with a sprung 6 mm push-button (3 mm travel, about 8 N). The button locks the leg at a hole when out and frees it when pressed; holes are 2.5 cm apart. The near leg's button faces the arms, 12 cm above the bench, and the seat rim above that leg is about 43 cm up. Distractors (SimReady): cleaning_soapDispenser_a01 at x 18, y 24; cleaning_brush_a01 at x 22, y -24. Neither is flat enough to shim a leg, and the scoring also requires bare feet on the bench.
concept.skill: One arm lifts the seat rim above the short leg about 3 cm and holds the chair level on its other three legs (about 1 kg at the rim). The other presses the 6 mm button inward with a fingertip, lets the inner tube slide down to the bench, and releases the button so it snaps into the next hole. Then the chair is lowered. Pressing the button while the chair rests on that leg drops the chair.
concept.scoring: From joint states and poses (real trial: count the holes, then a spirit level and a 1 mm feeler gauge under each foot). Latched: a leg's button is out and sits in a hole. Level: seat within 1 deg of horizontal. Steady: all four feet within 1 mm of the bench. End: grippers 3 cm or more from the chair, and the chair still for 1 s. Whole-run latch D: the chair dropped (any foot or the seat moving down faster than 0.3 m/s, as when a loaded leg is unlatched) or tipped beyond 20 deg. Score 0 if D is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 all four legs latched at the same hole, level and steady; 0.3 all four latched and the short leg moved, but not to the others' hole; 0 otherwise, including any leg left unlatched.
concept.nearest: 'Lengthen an adjustable walking stick to its red mark and lock it' and 'Add forearm-crutch-height task' (both rejected), and 'Extend a suitcase's handle to full height: keep its button pressed past the first stop' (pending), use the same push-button lock, but on an unloaded tube. 'Fold and secure a wall-mounted shower seat' (pending) is a different chair and skill. Here the hard part is taking the weight off a load-bearing leg with one arm while the other resets it.
concept.risks: Push-button telescoping is a familiar mechanism; reviewers may call this a variant of the stick and handle tasks unless the load and the drop are central to it. The seat rim (43 cm up) and the button (12 cm up) are within 10 cm of each other horizontally, so check that the two arms clear each other. The 2.2 kg chair rocking on rubber feet at friction 1.2 must settle into the faulted pose before the first step. The importance case rests on aides' bath set-up, so have fall statistics ready.

concept.title: Bring a resident's arm back through the side-rail opening it has slipped out of, supported at wrist and elbow, and rest it on the mattress
concept.justification: This is harm to a person. Limbs caught in side-rail openings (FDA entrapment zone 1) suffer skin tears, bruising and wrist injury, mostly in frail older patients. Pulling the hand back on its own bends the wrist past its range and drags the thin skin of the forearm across the bar. Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131, about 1.35M) and home health aides reposition residents' limbs many times a shift. The instruction only asks for the arm back on the bed. Supporting the joints, keeping the wrist neutral and lifting rather than dragging are left for the robot to work out.
concept.fault: A care-training manikin's right forearm lies out through an 11 cm opening between two rail bars. Its elbow is on the mattress just inside the rail, and its hand hangs outside the bed 20 cm below the rail top, wrist flexed 30 degrees, palm toward the bed.
concept.instruction: Her arm has slipped out through the bed rail. Put it back on the bed beside her.
concept.objects: Bed section, fixed, custom: a deck 10 cm above the bench with a 14 cm foam mattress in blue vinyl (top 24 cm up), spanning x 30 to 70, y -30 to 30. Half side rail in powder-coated steel and grey ABS along the mattress's near edge (x 28 to 30), y -25 to 25, top 22 cm above the mattress; its vertical bars are 2.5 cm wide and leave 11 cm openings. Torso block, fixed, out of reach at x 50 to 70. Manikin arm, adult female size, vinyl over a weighted core, built as a custom mechkit chain. Shoulder: 2 DOF, damped (0 to 45 deg abduction, -10 to 40 deg flexion). Upper arm: 29 cm, 1.4 kg. Elbow: revolute, 0 to 145 deg. Forearm: 24 cm, 0.9 kg, rotation -80 to 80 deg. Wrist: 2 DOF (flexion -70 to 60 deg, deviation +-25 deg). Hand: 18 cm, 0.4 kg. All joints are limp, with light damping and weak centring springs. Distractors (SimReady): thermometer_fever_a01 and dishware_plastic_cup_a01 on a fixed bedside tray at x 18, y -24; an oximeter_pulse prop at x 20, y 24.
concept.skill: Supporting a limb at two points through a narrow opening. One gripper cradles the forearm just above the wrist, outside the rail; the other supports the elbow inside. Together they raise the hand to the opening's height with the wrist kept neutral, draw the forearm in through the 11 cm gap without touching the bars, and lower the whole arm onto the mattress. A single grasp on the hand flexes the wrist past its range and drags the forearm across the bar.
concept.scoring: From joint angles and poses (real trial: video, with goniometer marks on the manikin). Whole-run harm latch H, set by any of: wrist flexion beyond 70 deg, extension beyond 60 or deviation beyond 25; elbow outside 0 to 145; forearm rotation beyond 80; any arm segment faster than 0.6 m/s (dropped); or the forearm or hand sliding along a rail bar (within 5 mm of it and moving faster than 5 cm/s) for more than 0.5 s in total. Inside: hand and forearm wholly on the mattress side of the rail's inner face. Resting: every arm segment within 2 cm above the mattress, and the forearm within 30 deg of parallel to the rail. End: grippers 3 cm or more from the arm, and the arm still for 1 s. Score 0 if H is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 inside and resting; 0.5 inside but not resting (draped over the rail or off the mattress edge); 0.2 hand back through the opening but forearm still across the rail; 0 otherwise.
concept.nearest: 'Rest a patient's cannulated forearm on an elevation wedge without dragging the IV line' and 'Scan a patient's wristband: roll the limp forearm over' (both pending); 'Straighten and hold a newborn training doll's two sprung legs flat while the other arm closes the footboard' (accepted); 'Give a patient's elbow one passive range-of-motion repetition' (rejected). None of them routes a limp limb back through an opening under joint-range limits.
concept.risks: The articulated limp arm is the hardest part to tune: a light hand at the end of chained joints, and parallel grippers that may slip on a round forearm. There is no SimReady manikin, so the arm and torso are custom meshes and must look like a training manikin, not capsules. The harm thresholds need cited range-of-motion norms. Reviewers may see it as close to the pending forearm tasks. The bar-sliding proxy must be tuned so a gentle touch is not penalised.

concept.title: Close the roller clamp on an IV line left running free, holding the clamp still while the wheel is rolled shut
concept.justification: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141, about 3.3M) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061, about 0.63M) close an IV set's roller clamp every time a set is primed, loaded, changed or stopped. A gravity line found running unclamped (free flow) is a recognised medication-error hazard. The clamp is a 54 mm, 6 g plastic body riding loose on soft tubing, so rolling its wheel with one hand only pushes the clamp and line along. A nurse pinches the body in one hand and thumbs the wheel with the other; a robot needs two grippers for the same thing.
concept.fault: A primed set hangs from a 1 L bag on a pole and runs across the overbed table to the cannula in a manikin's forearm. Its roller clamp lies on the table wide open, with the wheel at the open end, and the line is running free.
concept.instruction: Close the roller clamp on this IV line.
concept.objects: IV pole stub, fixed (as in the accepted Alaris task), at x 45, y -25, with a 1 L saline bag (custom mesh, 1.05 kg, fixed on its hook) and a rigid drip chamber. Administration-set tubing: PVC, 4.1 mm OD, a 60 cm capsule chain on the table (pattern from the accepted Alaris task, credited), anchored at the drip chamber outlet and at the cannula hub. Roller clamp, custom mechkit: a white polypropylene body 54 x 18 x 15 mm (mass raised to 15 g for the solver), welded to one tubing link and lying wheel-up at x 27, y -4. Its blue 11 mm wheel runs on a prismatic joint along a 22 mm sloped track, held by friction (about 4 N to roll), and counts as closed within 2 mm of the narrow stop. Manikin forearm with a taped cannula, fixed, at x 24, y 22. The bench is the overbed table. Distractors (SimReady): syringe_a01 at x 16, y -22; bandage_medical_a01 at x 38, y 8; thermometer_fever_a01 at x 15, y 10.
concept.skill: Fine two-handed manipulation. One gripper pins or pinches the 18 mm clamp body against the table near its tail. The other drives the 11 mm wheel 22 mm along its track with a fingertip, without lifting or dragging the clamp, which would tug the line on the patient's cannula.
concept.scoring: From poses and the wheel's joint (real trial: a photo of the wheel against the clamp's moulded stop). Whole-run latch P: the line between clamp and cannula pulled taut (its end-to-end length within 2 cm of its slack length), or the cannula-end link moved more than 5 mm. End: grippers 2 cm or more from clamp and tubing, everything still for 1 s. Score 0 if P is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 wheel within 2 mm of the closed stop; 0.4 wheel 60 percent or more of the way but not closed; 0 otherwise. Kinking or pinching the tube elsewhere earns nothing.
concept.nearest: 'Load an IV set into an Alaris pump module' (accepted) seats the same kind of set and presses its safety clamp into a recess. Also 'Add IV bag spiking and drip-chamber priming task' (revising) and 'Scrub the IV connector's hub for 15 seconds' (accepted). No existing task works a roller clamp's wheel.
concept.risks: The parts are at the gripper's limit (2 cm pads, an 11 mm wheel, an 18 mm body), and the two grippers work within 5 cm of each other. The soft tubing chain must stay stable with a light clamp welded to it. Reviewers may treat it as part of the IV-set family already covered. Fluid flow is not simulated, so closure is judged by the wheel position only.

concept.title: Shut off a dish-pit pre-rinse spray valve left locked on: steady the hanging head and slip its lock ring
concept.justification: Restaurant cooks (O*NET 35-2014, about 1.4M), food preparation workers (35-2021, about 0.9M) and dishwashers (35-9021, about 0.47M) use the pre-rinse spray valve over the dish-pit sink dozens of times a shift. They lock its squeeze handle on with the lock ring to fill pots and sinks hands-free. A valve left locked on keeps spraying 50-60 C water and moves about on its spring riser, and shutting it off is routine. Because the head hangs from a hose, pushing the ring with one hand just swings it away: one hand must steady and squeeze the head while the other slips the ring.
concept.fault: The valve hangs over the sink locked on. The lock ring holds its squeeze handle open, and the head hangs 18 cm above the drainboard, swinging gently.
concept.instruction: The pre-rinse sprayer has been left on. Turn it off and leave it hanging over the sink.
concept.objects: Pre-rinse unit, custom mechkit. The riser and overhead spring are fixed out of reach (anchor at x 42, y -10, 75 cm up). The hose is a damped two-link pendulum (spherical joint at the anchor, 55 cm in total) ending in a chrome spray valve 15 cm long, 0.45 kg. Squeeze handle: a sprung revolute, off at rest, about 12 N to hold open. Lock ring: a 2.5 cm steel loop on a revolute with a detent. Hooked over the handle tip it holds the handle open; it comes off only when the handle is squeezed a little further and the ring is pushed down off the tip. Valve rest point: x 26, y -10, 18 cm up. Stainless sink and drainboard, fixed, custom (fixture_sink_basin_a01 if its size fits). Optional: a 2 N reaction force along the nozzle while the valve is open, applied in on_step. Distractors (SimReady): kitchenware_pan_a01 upside down on the drainboard at x 16, y 18; cleaning_sponge_c01 at x 38, y 20; dishware_plastic_bigPlate_a01 at x 14, y -24.
concept.skill: Catch and hold a hanging, swinging 0.45 kg head without yanking its hose. Squeeze body and handle together in one gripper to unload the ring, and push the ring off the handle tip with the other. Then let the head swing back and settle with no gripper on it.
concept.scoring: From joint states and poses (real trial: whether water is flowing, and where the head hangs). Shut: handle at its off stop and the ring off. Hanging: head within 8 cm of its rest point and not touching the sink or drainboard. End: grippers 3 cm or more from head and hose, and the head under 3 cm/s for 2 s. Whole-run latch Y: the head pulled more than 20 cm below its rest point (hose overstretched), or struck the sink faster than 0.8 m/s. Score 0 if Y is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 shut and hanging; 0.4 shut but left lying on the drainboard or in the sink; 0 if still locked on.
concept.nearest: 'Set a garden hose wand from Jet to Shower: hold the wand by its handle while the other hand clicks the dial round' (pending) holds a sprayer while changing its setting. 'Rinse a glass on a bar's push-down glass rinser' (accepted) uses a different valve. 'Add lock-the-trigger-before-swapping-a-pressure-washer-nozzle task' (rejected); 'Steady a swinging conveyor carrier before lifting a tin out of it' (closed). No pre-rinse unit appears in the known tasks.
concept.risks: Water and its reaction force are not simulated, or are a scripted force. Reviewers may call the swinging an invented event, so keep it gentle and explain it. Dishwashers alone are under 500,000, so the claim rests on cooks and prep workers. The pendulum hose and the ring detent need tuning for stability. The closest pending task (the garden wand) shares 'hold a sprayer, work its control'.

concept.title: Free a kitchen drawer that a ladle has jammed a few centimetres open, holding the ladle down through the gap while drawing the drawer out
concept.justification: Almost everyone has had a utensil drawer stop a few centimetres open because a ladle or whisk has tipped up and caught under the worktop; cooks and home care aides meet it in their work too. Pulling harder bends the utensil or breaks the drawer front. What works is easing the drawer back, reaching through the gap with a flat utensil to press the handle down, and drawing the drawer out while keeping it pressed. The jam cannot be seen from above and the gap is 2 cm high, so the work is done by feel, with two hands.
concept.fault: A ladle in the drawer lies across a spatula and tips 15 degrees up toward the front, because its bowl end is heavier. Its hooked handle end catches the back of the worktop's front rail, so the drawer opens only 2.5 cm. When released, the handle rises again.
concept.instruction: This drawer is stuck. Open it all the way.
concept.objects: Kitchen base cabinet section, fixed, custom: a white melamine carcass 50 cm wide under a 3 cm laminate worktop (underside 16 cm above the bench, front edge at x 20, 2 cm overhang), with a 2 cm deep front rail beneath the worktop. The drawer runs on a mechkit prismatic joint (full-extension ball-bearing slide, 0 to 40 cm, light damping). Its box is 44 x 40 x 9 cm inside; its front is 50 x 13 x 1.8 cm with a stainless bar pull 7 cm up, leaving a 2 cm slot between the front's top edge and the worktop. Loose in the drawer (SimReady): kitchenware_ladle_a01 (0.17 kg), kitchenware_spatula_b01 (the fulcrum under the ladle), kitchenware_spoon_b01, kitchenware_fork_a01. Available on the worktop: kitchenware_spatula_c01 (a thin turner). Distractors on the worktop (SimReady): dishware_mug_a01 at x 34, y 18; food_produce_apple_a01 at x 32, y -20.
concept.skill: Blind, two-handed work through a narrow gap. One arm eases the drawer back to unload the wedge, and later draws it out by its pull. The other slides a flat turner in through the 2 cm slot, levers the ladle handle down against the drawer front's edge, and keeps it down while the drawer comes out past the rail. If the handle is released early it springs back up and jams again.
concept.scoring: From poses (real trial: a tape measure along the drawer side). Open: drawer 35 cm or more out, of 40. Contents: the ladle and the other three utensils all inside the drawer box. Score: 1.0 open with all contents inside; 0.4 drawer out 8 cm or more (past the jam) but not fully, with all contents inside; 0 otherwise, including any utensil flicked out of the drawer.
concept.nearest: 'Safety and alignment: bimanual recovery from a clothing-obstructed drawer' (rejected). 'Take a drawer out of its slides by pressing two opposite-sense release levers while pulling' and 'Refit a loaded drawer on its roller slides' (both accepted). 'Push a peg home past a hidden obstruction without forcing it' (accepted). RoboCasa opens drawers but never jammed ones.
concept.risks: A reviewer may recall the rejected clothing-drawer task; what differs is the rigid ladle and the lever action. Pulling hard does nothing in simulation, but in reality it bends the ladle; no force is measured, so the scoring cannot penalise forcing, which fidelity must say. Inserting a flat tool horizontally through a 2 cm slot with a top-down gripper is tight, so check it offline. The top camera cannot see the jam, by design. The category is Societal relatability rather than jobs.

concept.title: Lift an infusion pump that has slid down its IV pole back to the tape mark and turn its pole clamp tight
concept.justification: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131, about 1.35M, whose tasks include 'set up equipment') and registered nurses (29-1141, about 3.3M) mount infusion pumps on poles and move them between poles at every transfer. A pole clamp that is not turned tight lets the 1.4 kg pump slide down and swing round, dragging its line and leaving the pole top-heavy at the wrong height. Fixing it takes two hands: one holds the pump at height and square, while the other turns the clamp knob, whose torque also tries to twist the pump.
concept.fault: The pump has slid down to the pole's lower collar, 8 cm above the bench, and turned 35 degrees about the pole. Its clamp knob is two turns loose.
concept.instruction: This pump has slipped down its pole. Fix it back at the tape mark with its screen facing you.
concept.objects: IV pole stub, fixed (like the accepted Alaris task's stub): chromed steel tube 25 mm across, from the bench to 60 cm, at x 33, y 0, with blue tape from 24 to 26 cm and a steel collar at 8 cm. Infusion pump: SimReady pump_infusion_a01 at real size (about 20 x 13 x 22 cm, grey ABS, carry handle on top), mass set to 1.4 kg; replace it with a custom mesh if the asset's shape is unsuitable. Pole clamp, custom mechkit, on the pump's back. The pump rides the pole on a prismatic joint (vertical) and a revolute joint (about the pole). Their friction drives scale with clamp tightness: free below half a turn past contact, locked from 1.5 turns. The knob has four lobes, is 6 cm across, sits on the pump's left side with its axis along the clamp screw (horizontal), and turns on a damped revolute. Distractors (SimReady): syringe_a02 at x 16, y -22; device_blood_pressure_monitor_a01 at x 18, y 24; disinfectant_b01 at x 40, y -24.
concept.skill: One arm holds a 1.4 kg device by its carry handle (top-down) at a set height and square, against gravity and against the knob's twisting torque. The other turns the knob three turns by pressing its lobes down one after another and regrasping, like turning a wheel by its spokes.
concept.scoring: From poses and the knob's joint (real trial: a ruler to the tape, a protractor on the pump face, and a hand check that it does not slide). Locked: knob 1.5 turns or more past contact. On mark: clamp centre within 1.5 cm of the tape centre. Facing: screen within 10 deg of facing the arms. End: grippers 3 cm or more from pump and pole, and the pump moving under 2 mm and 1 deg over 3 s. Whole-run latch F: the pump fell (downward faster than 0.6 m/s) or left the pole. Score 0 if F is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 locked, on mark and facing; 0.5 locked within 6 cm and 30 deg; 0.2 locked anywhere else; 0 not locked.
concept.nearest: 'Load an IV set into an Alaris pump module' (accepted) works on a pump that is already clamped to a pole stub. 'Add clamp-a-flask-on-a-lab-stand task' (pending) tightens a clamp on a vertical rod. 'Fix a copper tube in two self-closing pipe clamps' (rejected). This task re-clamps the device's own clamp while holding its weight.
concept.risks: This is the weakest of the eight. Its skill is close to the pending lab-stand clamp, and reviewers may call mounting a pump a supporting activity. Turning a horizontal-axis knob by pressing its lobes top-down is plausible, but it is not how a nurse turns one. 1.4 kg is near the arm's payload with the arm reaching upward. The SimReady pump's geometry is unknown until it is checked with simready_info.py.

concept.title: Get a countertop drinks cooler's self-closing door to seal when a bottle left overhanging the deck is holding it ajar
concept.justification: Stockers and order fillers (O*NET 53-7065, about 2.8M US jobs) fill and face reach-in and countertop coolers every shift. Convenience-store cashiers (41-2011, about 3.3M) restock the countertop cooler by the till between sales. Store audits most often flag a door held ajar by product left too far forward: the drinks warm and the coil frosts. Holding the sprung door off a bottle while setting the bottle back is core, regular cooler work for both occupations.
concept.fault: Six bottles stand on the cooler deck. The front-right bottle stands 25 mm past the deck's front edge; it is still balanced. The self-closing door rests against it, 6 deg open, with its free edge 40 mm off the gasket.
concept.instruction: Get the cooler door shut and sealed, with all six bottles standing inside.
concept.objects: Countertop glass-door merchandiser, fixed (mechkit fixed frame). Cabinet: white powder-coated steel, 440 W x 400 D x 480 H mm; inside 400 x 340 x 400 mm; deck 30 mm above the table; front face at x 0.24, centred on y 0. Door: mechkit hinge link on a vertical axis at the left front corner (y +0.20). It is 400 x 400 mm double-glazed glass in a black ABS frame, 2.6 kg, with a 25 mm recessed pull along the top of its free edge. Closing spring 0.8 N m/rad, with its rest set 3 deg past closed by set_target to give a preload, plus damping. A fixed wall stops the door at 45 deg, so it has no 90 deg hold-open. 'Sealed' means the door is within 0.5 deg of closed. Six 500 ml PET water bottles: SimReady food_beverage_bottledWater_f01 (62 x 165 mm, mass set to 0.53 kg), in two rows of three at 70 mm pitch. Distractors on the counter, each at least 6 cm from the task: handheld barcode scanner (computer_scanner_barcode_b01), paper coffee cup (food_beverage_coffeeCup_a01), chocolate bar (food_processed_chocolate_a01).
concept.skill: One arm pulls the door open by its top pull, turning its yaw to follow the arc, against a 0.8 N m/rad spring. It holds the door 25-35 deg open. The other arm reaches in through the opening and pushes the overhanging bottle 30-40 mm back, square on the deck, without tipping it into its neighbour, then withdraws. The first arm then lets the door swing shut under control. Two arms are needed for three reasons: the door swings back onto the bottle the moment it is let go; the bottle cannot be reached through the 40 mm gap behind the glass; and the stop keeps the door short of any hold-open.
concept.scoring: Scored from poses and the door joint. On a real cooler, use a feeler card at the gasket and a photo. Sealed: door within 0.5 deg of closed for 2 s. In: every bottle upright (tilt 10 deg or less), its base on the deck and wholly 10 mm or more behind the deck's front edge. Released: every fingertip point 3 cm or more from the door and bottles, everything still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Whole-run harm latch: any bottle ever tilted past 45 deg, left the deck, or fell off the counter. Score 0 if the latch is set. 1.0: sealed, all six in, released. 0.5: sealed, five in, and the overhanging bottle standing upright on the counter outside (not restocked). 0.25: all six in, but the door not sealed (still held, or more than 0.5 deg ajar). 0: anything else, including doing nothing.
concept.nearest: Accepted 'Restock a spring-pusher shelf lane behind the older stock, holding the pusher back' (holds a sprung part back while placing stock). Pending 'Hand a drink out a self-closing drive-thru window: hold the slider, set the cup on the outside shelf, let it shut clear'. Accepted 'Take one bottle from a row of five without knocking any over'. Rejected 'Add reclose-vaccine-cooler task'. RoboCasa has open/close fridge-door tasks, but none with a sprung door pressing on the item to be moved. Here the sprung part is a hinged door whose arc must be tracked, the item to move is the one the door presses on, and success is a seal, not a placement.
concept.risks: Holding a sprung part while acting is a known pattern (spring pusher, drive-thru window), so reviewers may see it as a variant. Demos are top-down only, so the pushing gripper's wrist must fit inside a 400 mm-high cabinet through the door opening; check IK first. The door's arc passes within about 20 cm of the right arm base. A 2.6 kg door on a preloaded sprung joint and glass rendering need testing. At the default friction of 1.2 a pushed bottle may tip, so set PET on steel to about 0.3. The door-top pull is about 0.45 m above the table, near the upper reach.

concept.title: Restack a full bail-arm tote that has sunk into the full tote below because one bail was left down
concept.justification: Two occupations stack and unstack full stack-nest totes all shift in distribution centres and store backrooms: stockers and order fillers (53-7065, about 2.8M) and hand laborers and freight, stock and material movers (53-7062, about 3.0M). Bail-arm containers stack on two swung-in wire bails and nest when the bails are swung out. A bail left out lets the next full tote drop into the one below and onto its stock. This is the everyday mis-seated-tote fault, and a stack like that cannot go on a dolly or a conveyor. Stacking totes is core, regular work in both occupations.
concept.fault: Lower tote: its near-end bail hangs down outside the near end wall (nest position); its far bail lies across the top (stack position). The full upper tote rests on the far bail at its far end. Its near end has dropped about 30 mm below the lower tote's rim onto the bags of crisps inside, so the upper tote is tilted about 6 deg.
concept.instruction: Make the two totes a proper stack, with nothing spilled.
concept.objects: Two grey polypropylene Euro stack-nest containers, 400 x 300 x 150 mm, 0.9 kg each, with 3 deg wall draft and 100 x 30 mm end handholds. Each has two 6 mm zinc-plated steel-wire bail arms (U shape, 75 mm legs, 290 mm crossbar, 0.09 kg) pivoting on the end walls 20 mm below the rim. Build each tote as a mechkit mechanism with a free frame (free_mass) and two gravity hinge links (0 to 175 deg; the stack position rests in rim notches at 0). The lower tote stands on the table with its long axis along x (x 0.12 to 0.52), centred on y 0; the upper tote sits above it. Contents: the lower tote holds 4 bags of crisps (SimReady food_processed_chips_a01-d01, 0.15 kg each, tops 25 mm below the rim). The upper tote holds 6 boxed foods lying flat (SimReady food_processed_boxedFood_a01-f01, 0.12 kg each); the upper tote totals about 1.6 kg. Distractors: retractable box cutter (handTool_knife_retractableBlade_a01), roll of clear tape (tape_clear_a01), handheld scanner (computer_scanner_barcode_b01).
concept.skill: One arm lifts the sunk near end of the 1.6 kg tote by its end handhold, about 90 mm, out of the partial nest. It must lift straight, or the tapered walls drag; the tote pivots on the far bail, so the hand carries about 0.8 kg. That arm holds the end up. The other arm pinches the hanging bail's crossbar and swings it 180 deg up over the rim into its stack notch, under the raised end. The first arm then lowers the tote onto the bail. Two arms are needed because the bail's arc passes exactly under the end that must be held up. Lifting the whole full tote off by one handhold would tip its contents.
concept.scoring: Scored from poses and the bail joints; on a real stack, use a photo and a ruler. Stacked: both bails within 8 deg of their stack notches; the upper tote resting on both bails, with all four bottom corners within 6 mm of the stacked height; tilt 2 deg or less; centre within 15 mm and yaw within 5 deg of the lower tote's. Released: fingertips 3 cm or more from both totes and all bails, everything still (under 1 cm/s and 2 deg/s) for 1 s. Whole-run harm latch H, set if: any product item is ever outside its tote's walls; the upper tote ever tilts past 30 deg or falls (any corner below the lower rim, outside the lower tote); or the lower tote moves more than 3 cm or tips more than 5 deg. Score 0 with H. 1.0: stacked, released, still. 0.4: the upper tote is off the stack and standing level (3 deg or less) on the table, both lower bails are in stack position, released and still (the load is made safe but the stack is not rebuilt). 0.2: at the end, the upper tote's bottom is 10 mm or more clear of the crisps everywhere, but it is not stacked. 0: anything else, including doing nothing.
concept.nearest: Rejected 'Add task: Put each empty tote on the tote behind it so it stacks on the full one and nests in the empty one' (choosing the orientation of an empty rotate-stack tote; no mechanism, no fault). Rejected 'Add fold-retail-basket-handle: Fold a retail hand basket's bow handle down flat' (folds the handle of an empty basket). Accepted 'Carry a stack of three boxes onto a shelf in one trip, squeezed between both arms' and 'Release a two-latch lid and lift it out with both hands' (two-arm lifts; nothing is swung under a held load). Our own draft 'Put a knocked-out prop back under a loaded shelf board' also restores a support under a load, but slides a loose prop in. Here the support is a hinge on the container itself, swung through an arc past the rim while a loaded, tapered tote is held up out of a partial nest.
concept.risks: Overlaps our team's support-under-load drafts (reseat-shelf-prop, remove-prop); reviewers may call it the same skill. Bail-arm containers are most common at 600 x 400; the 400 x 300 size exists, but its dimensions need checking. A free articulated tote whose hinge links carry another free 1.6 kg tote must be tested for solver stability; give the bails real mass and gravity. The near end, at x 0.12 and 0.25 to 0.40 m above the table, is near the arm's inner reach. At friction 1.2 the tapered nest binds, so set PP to about 0.4. The boxes may slide at 15 to 20 deg of tilt.

concept.title: Refit a produce bin's front dam that has jumped out of one socket, keeping the apples pressing on it in the bin
concept.justification: Stockers and order fillers (53-7065, about 2.8M) include the produce clerks who build, rotate and cull produce displays all shift. Angled produce bins hold their fruit with a clear front dam whose end pins drop into sockets. A dam knocked out at one end, by a cart, a customer or a carton, lets fruit roll off and bruise, and the bruised fruit is written off. Refitting the dam while the fruit leans on it is routine produce work.
concept.fault: The dam's right pin is out of its socket. Pivoting on its left pin, the dam's right end has dropped onto the bin's front lip, leaning 30 deg forward. Five apples on the right rest against it, and two of them are already past the lip line.
concept.instruction: Put the front dam back in both of its sockets, with every apple still in the bin.
concept.objects: Produce bin, fixed: a 560 W x 360 D mm black ABS false bottom tilted 15 deg down toward the robot (front edge at x 0.14, 80 mm above the table), with 90 mm side walls, a 20 mm front lip, and two chrome sockets, 8 mm bore and 25 mm deep, at the front corners (y +-0.27). Dam: clear acrylic, 540 x 70 x 6 mm, with a 6 mm chrome pin 30 mm long at each end, 0.22 kg; a mechkit free part with convex colliders. 18 apples: SimReady food_produce_apple_* (about 75 mm, mass set to 0.18 kg), in three loose rows. Distractors: a bunch of bananas in a separate bin to the left (food_produce_banana_bunch_a01), a roll of produce bags (paper_roll_a01), and a price card on a clip stand.
concept.skill: One arm holds the five right-hand apples back up the slope with the flat of its closed fingers, as a moving wall rather than a grasp, and keeps them there. The other arm lifts the dam's right end by its top edge, swings it upright about the left pin, and drops the 6 mm pin into the 8 mm socket in front of the held apples. The first arm then eases off so the apples settle against the seated dam. Two arms are needed because released apples roll off the 15 deg slope, and a dam lifted without holding them lets them roll under it.
concept.scoring: Seated: both pins in their sockets (pin tips within 3 mm of the socket floors) and the dam within 3 deg of upright. In the bin: an apple's centre is inside the bin's inner walls and above the false bottom. Whole-run fall count: each apple whose centre ever drops 30 mm below the top of the front lip outside the bin, or reaches the table. Released: fingertips 3 cm or more from the dam and apples, and every apple under 1 cm/s for 1 s. 1.0: seated, none fallen, released, still. 0.5: seated, exactly one fallen. 0.2: dam not seated, but none fallen and every apple behind the lip line (made safe). 0: anything else; doing nothing scores 0 because two apples start past the lip line.
concept.nearest: Accepted 'Pull a reject bin from the middle of a gravity flow lane without letting the next bin run down' (holds back one bin on rollers while lifting another out). Accepted 'Face cans to the shelf edge'. Accepted 'Unload fruit from a bin another robot arm is also unloading'. Rejected 'Add Restock a flow lane first-in, first-out task'. None refits a restraint: here a loose pile of rolling fruit is held back with an open hand while a dam is refitted by its pins in front of it.
concept.risks: Close to the flow lane's hold-back skill, so reviewers may call it a variant. Many convex-hull apples on a slope cost contact time and may jitter, and spheres may keep rolling; set produce on ABS to about 0.6. A gripper used as a paddle may let apples squeeze past it. Real produce tables are larger, so claim only one bin of a display at its real size.

concept.title: Free a coin roll wedged under the front of a loaded till so the cash drawer shuts and latches, spilling no coins
concept.justification: Cashiers (41-2011, about 3.3M), and retail salespersons (41-2031) who work registers, open and shut the cash drawer for every cash sale and break coin rolls into the till several times a shift. A roll that slips under the till's front lip lifts the till. The till then catches on the housing and the drawer's kick spring sends it back open, leaving cash exposed. Clearing the jam without dumping the coin cups is routine register work.
concept.fault: The drawer is open, sprung out 260 mm. A wrapped roll of 40 quarters lies across the media slot under the till's front lip and lifts the till's front 25 mm (about 5 deg). When pushed in, the till's front edge catches the housing's top front edge 20 mm short of the latch, and the kick spring returns the drawer.
concept.instruction: The cash drawer won't stay shut. Get it closed and latched without spilling any coins.
concept.objects: POS cash drawer: black steel housing, 410 W x 415 D x 100 H mm, fixed, front at x 0.42, centred on y 0. Drawer: a mechkit slider (0 to 0.30 m) with a 6 N kick-open spring. The latch is a mechkit lock that engages when travel is 1 mm or less; it is released only by the drawer's solenoid, which never fires during a run. Till insert: black ABS tray, 370 x 310 x 60 mm, 0.45 kg. It has five bill slots with bill stacks (thin slabs) under sprung bill-weight clips (visual only). Five round coin cups along its front hold coin stacks as loose short cylinders: quarters 24.3 mm, nickels 21.2, pennies 19.0, dimes 17.9 mm. The till weighs about 1.2 kg in all. Coin roll: brown kraft-wrapped cylinder, 26 x 69 mm, 0.227 kg, loose. Distractors: a receipt-printer housing (box), a handheld scanner (computer_scanner_barcode_b01), a pen.
concept.skill: One arm lifts the till's front lip about 30 mm and draws it 10 mm back off the roll, keeping the till within 8 deg so the coin stacks stay in their cups. The other arm plucks the roll out of the slot and sets it aside. The first arm lowers the till flat into its seat. Then one arm pushes the drawer home against its kick spring until the latch catches. Two arms are needed because the roll is trapped under the till's lip, and a till lifted high enough by one hand to free a roll tips the coins out of its cups.
concept.scoring: Latched: drawer travel 1 mm or less with the latch engaged, held for 2 s. Seated: till tilt 1 deg or less, all four feet within 2 mm of the drawer floor. Roll clear: the roll's centre outside the till's footprint. Whole-run spill latch S: any coin stack ever leaves its cup or tips past 45 deg. Released: fingertips 3 cm or more from the drawer and till at the end, everything still for 1 s. 1.0: latched, seated, roll clear, no S, released. 0.5: roll clear, till seated, no S, drawer not latched. 0.25: latched, seated and roll clear, but S happened. 0: anything else, including doing nothing.
concept.nearest: Pending 'Add swap-the-counted-till-insert-into-the-cash-drawer task' (lifts a till out and in). Accepted 'Take a drawer out of its slides by pressing two opposite-sense release levers while pulling'. Accepted 'Refit a loaded drawer on its roller slides, carried in above riding height so the rear hooks clear, then pull-test it'. Rejected 'Add till-make-change'. RoboCasa's drawer-closing tasks have no latch, kick spring or jam. Here the till stays in the drawer: only its front edge is lifted, under a spill limit, to clear a jam, and then the drawer must latch against its kick spring.
concept.risks: It uses the same objects as the pending till swap, so it may be judged a near-duplicate. It is also close to our draft 'Get a spirit level out from under a loose riser shelf', which lifts a loaded part to free something under it. Representing coins as stacked cylinders is a simplification. A top-down gripper must reach under the raised till lip to grip the roll; check the clearance. The kick spring and the lock must not fight a push at the latch point.

concept.title: Reseat a checkout scanner-scale's weigh plate that was put back after cleaning riding on its frame lip
concept.justification: Cashiers (41-2011, about 3.3M) weigh produce on the scanner-scale for nearly every grocery order and wipe its weigh plate every shift. Put back with one side on the counter frame, the plate touches the frame and the scale under-weighs, which breaks weights-and-measures law and loses the store money on every weighed sale. Cashiers reseat the plate so it floats clear all round.
concept.fault: The 400 x 290 mm stainless weigh plate sits with its left side up on the frame's 6 mm lip, tilted about 1 deg and touching the frame. Its right side rests on its supports.
concept.instruction: Put the scale's weigh plate back so it sits properly in its frame.
concept.objects: Checkstand section, fixed: a laminate counter top with a stainless-framed recess, 406 x 296 mm, giving 3 mm clearance all round. Inside are four rubber-capped load-receptor pins, 10 mm below the counter. Behind the recess's rear edge stands the scanner tower, a fixed black box 400 x 120 x 180 mm with a glass window. Weigh plate: 3 mm stainless steel with 15 mm upturned side lips (where it is lifted), a 25 mm produce rail at the rear, and a sapphire window in the centre (visual), 1.4 kg; a mechkit free part. Its long axis runs along y (y +-0.20, x 0.15 to 0.44). Distractors: a bunch of bananas at the belt end (food_produce_banana_bunch_a01), a can of soup (food_canned_soup_a01), a receipt card.
concept.skill: Each arm pinches one side lip; together they lift the 1.4 kg, 400 mm plate level off the frame lip and shift it 4 mm across. They then lower it straight down into a recess with 3 mm clearance per side, so that no edge touches the frame and it lands on all four pins at once. Two arms are needed because a plate lifted by one lip tilts, and a one-sided lowering wedges the far edge on the frame lip.
concept.scoring: Seated: all four corners on their pins (within 1 mm of seated height), plate tilt 0.3 deg or less, and a gap of 1 mm or more to the frame on all four sides (no contact). Released: fingertips 3 cm or more from the plate, plate still for 1 s. Whole-run drop latch: the plate ever moved down faster than 0.4 m/s, or its edge struck the tower window faster than 0.2 m/s. 1.0: seated, released, still, no drop. 0.4: flat on its pins (tilt 0.3 deg or less) but touching the frame on one side, released, still, no drop (the scale still reads wrong). 0: anything else (still on the lip, held, dropped, or off the counter).
concept.nearest: Accepted 'Add refit-a-gas-burner-head-and-cap task' (a cleaned part seated by sight). Pending 'Refit a fridge door bin: carry it in level above its two hidden supports, lower both ends on together, push it home'. Rejected 'Run a bench scale's eccentricity test: a 1 kg weight on the centre and four corner points of an unmarked platter'. Revising 'Add scan-four-groceries-across-a-checkout-scanner task'. Here a wide plate must be lowered level into a close-clearance recess so that it floats clear of the frame on every side.
concept.risks: Reviewers may judge it ordinary pick-and-place (the difficulty not robotic), and may call wiping the plate a supporting activity. The 3 mm clearance and the no-contact check need care with PhysX contact offsets. A thin plate can only be lifted top-down by its lips; make sure real plates have such lips or a lift rail.

concept.title: Put a novelty freezer's sliding glass lid back in both tracks and slide it shut after it was knocked off its rear track
concept.justification: Stockers and order fillers (53-7065) in grocery and convenience stores, and convenience-store cashiers (41-2011), stock ice-cream chest freezers with sliding glass lids every shift. Customers knock a lid off its rear track. It then lies cocked across the opening and cannot slide shut, so the freezer stays open and the stock softens. Staff lift the lid back into both tracks and close it.
concept.fault: The right-hand lid's rear edge is out of the rear track, resting on the rim 15 mm up and 20 mm forward. Its front edge is still in the front track. The lid is tilted about 3 deg and stands 120 mm open.
concept.instruction: Close the freezer's right-hand lid properly.
concept.objects: The top of a full-size novelty chest freezer at counter height; the table stands in for the cabinet below, and every part is full size. White rim, fixed, with front and rear aluminium U-tracks 6 mm deep, two grooves each; the front track at x 0.15, the rear at x 0.47; the lids slide along y. Under them is a wire basket of boxed novelties (SimReady food_processed_boxedFood_*). Distractors: a price sign on the rim, a paper coffee cup (food_beverage_coffeeCup_a01) on the counter.

Together they lift the 1.4 kg, 300 mm-wide glass lid level and set its rear edge down into the rear groove while the front edge stays in the front groove. They then slide it 120 mm along both tracks to its stop, keeping it square so it does not rack and bind. Two arms are needed because a lid lifted at one end tilts and drops its other edge, and a lid pushed at one corner racks in the tracks.
concept.scoring: In tracks: the front and rear frame edges both below their track lips, in the right-hand grooves. Shut: the lid within 5 mm of its end stop. Flat: tilt 1 deg or less. Whole-run drop latch: the lid ever fell into the freezer or onto the stock (moving down faster than 0.4 m/s), or left the rim. Released: fingertips 3 cm or more from the lid, lid still for 1 s. 1.0: in tracks, shut, flat, released, no drop. 0.5: in tracks and flat but not shut. 0: anything else.
concept.nearest: Rejected 'Open a sliding door jammed by a block in its track'. Rejected 'Slide a clear panel along the top and bottom slots of an aluminium frame to its end stop by its pull knob'. Rejected 'Add wardrobe-sliding-doors task'. Closed 'Add task: Take a pack from the back of a chest freezer whose lid is stopped part open by a wall cupboard'. Here a glass lid must be engaged in two tracks at once and then slid without racking.
concept.risks: The sliding-panel family has been rejected several times, so reviewers may see little new. Building only the top of a full-size freezer must be argued the way the accepted gas-hob corner was. The rear track is near the reach limit. concept.title: Rehang a full parts bin left perched on its louvered panel's crest instead of hooked behind it
concept.justification: Stockers and order fillers (53-7065, about 2.8M) in industrial-supply, auto-parts and hardware stockrooms pick from and refill hang-on bins on louvered panels all shift. A bin put back with its hanging rib on the louver's crest looks hung, but it falls when a part is pulled from it and spills the fasteners. Rehanging bins is routine stockroom work.
concept.fault: A 280 x 150 x 130 mm blue hang-on bin holding 1.1 kg of M8 bolts and nuts sits with its rear hanging rib on top of a louver's crest. It is tilted 6 deg back and stands 5 mm proud of its two neighbours.
concept.instruction: Hang the bolt bin on the panel properly, with nothing spilled.
concept.objects: Louvered steel panel, fixed, grey, 600 W x 450 H mm, vertical at x 0.47, with louvers every 63 mm, each with a 10 mm upturned lip. Three blue polypropylene hang-on bins, 280 D x 150 W x 130 H mm, 0.25 kg each, with a 12 mm rear hanging rib and a hopper front (mechkit free parts with convex colliders). The two neighbouring bins are hung correctly and hold M8 nuts. Contents of the faulty bin: SimReady factory_bolt_m8_loose and factory_nut_m8_loose, about 25 of each, with masses set so they total 1.1 kg. Distractors on the bench below: a tape dispenser (misc_tape_dispenser_a01) and a cloth (cleaning_cloth_a01).

They then lower it so the rib drops behind the lip, keeping the bin within 15 deg so the bolts stay in.
